reviewer_note: TET0128: original spelling is Tetranychus hypogaeae Gupta, 1976. Keep distinct from Eotetranychus hypogeae Karuppuchamy & Mohanasundaram, 1988.

Retain Mixonychus (Tylonychus) jayaraji (Karuppuchamy & Mohanasundaram, 1987). Correct Tylonicus to Tylonychus. Preserve Tetranychus jayaraji as an erroneous source usage, not an independently described species.
Retain the distinct combretis and combretus identities. Host overlap does not support synonymy. Do not change Levonga to Colopodacus.
Use Acalitus ruelliae (Channabasavanna, 1966). Retain the older Aceria combination in synonym/source history.
Phaicus bambusae (Channabasavanna, 1966) needs parentheses. Its original name is Tegolophus bambusae (1966:122-123); Aceria bambusae was described on pp. 58-59. Do not merge these species.

Merge the catalogue records while retaining both spellings and original attributions in source history. Wang 1964 has priority. Sources differ in sacchari/saccharini usage; the decision does not settle the accepted spelling or all sugarcane field identifications.
Use Aculus leguminae (Mohanasundaram, 1982); retain Aculops as the original combination.
Use Aculus shoreum (Ghosh, Mondal & Chakrabarti, 1986). Source-book original-combination wording conflicts between Phyllocoptes and Aculops; retain that discrepancy for bibliographic correction.

Keep the Nalepa identity and check 1914 as the original year. Do not merge it with the separately attributed alangii Mohanasundaram, 1981, for which the source book gives the replacement name Eriophyes coimbatoriensis. This decision concerns the two Nalepa-attributed rows.

Eriophyes antiquorum should carry the replacement-name authorship Amrine & Stasny, 1994. Do not carry Mohanasundaram as the author of that replacement name, and do not merge with Proneotegonotus antiquorae.
Use Eriophyes casuarinae Channabasavanna, 1966; retain Phytoptus casuarinae as historical source usage.

Do not retain Mohanasundaram, 1981 as independent species authorship. Link this usage to the Wang 1964 sugarcane blister-mite record. Inference from the publication history; the complete 1981 paper and Halliday full text were not available. Do not generalize this merge to unidentified rice/sugarcane samples.
Use Mesalox odayarae (Mohanasundaram, 1980). Standardize Mohansundaram to Mohanasundaram in the older entry.

ERI0536 corresponds to Tegolophus mohanasundarami Amrine & Stasny, 1994, the replacement name reported for T. gmelinae Mohanasundaram, 1983. If mohanasundarami already has a catalogue row, check that separate duplicate. Keep gmelinus distinct.
Retain separate taxon identities. Check the homonymy / any replacement name for the Kar & Karmakar species before choosing its final display name.
Keep both author-year identities. Matching orientalis does not make these taxa synonyms.

Supply 2003 for the Chatterjee & Gupta record. The 2015 checklist reports indica as its replacement name for a junior homonym; verify the accepted genus before renaming. Generic placement of the Ghai & Menon taxon varies between sources.
Retain Gupta & Ray, 1981 separately from Gupta, 1981. Do not replace one authority with the other during standardization.
Use Okiseius laaensis (Gupta, 1986). The Paraphytoseius placement in the extracted list is a generic placement/transcription issue; preserve the source usage without counting an extra species.
Replacement name for T. gmelinae Mohanasundaram, 1983 (IRMNG); confirmed by V. K. Chaudhari
indica replaces the junior homonym Amblyseius (Typhlodromalus) mangiferae Chatterjee & Gupta, 2003 (Gupta & Karmakar 2015, entry 116)

Paraphytoseius multidentatus Swirski & Shechter, 1961 is a junior synonym of P. orientalis (Narayanan, Kaur & Ghai, 1960): Chant & McMurtry 2003, International Journal of Acarology 29(3):179-224, p. 220; followed by Moraes et al. 2004 and Lofego et al. 2024 (Zootaxa 5439). Matthysse & Denmark 1981 (Florida Entomologist 64(2):340-357, p. 342) had treated P. multidentatus as the senior name. Gupta & Karmakar 2015 list both, as Amblyseiulella multidentatus and A. orientalis; Gupta 1985 lists Amblyseius (Paraphytoseius) multidentatus.

Eriophyes euphorbiae Mohanasundaram, 1983 (on Euphorbia antiquorum, Tamil Nadu; Dyamanagouda et al. 2020) is preoccupied; Eriophyes antiquorum Amrine & Stasny, 1994 is its replacement name (Mohammad-Doustaresharaf et al. 2023, Persian Journal of Acarology 12(1):81-89). Gupta & Mondal 2023 list the same mite from the same host and state as E. antiquorum. One species.
